title: A RECORD OF WHAT GOD DID

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: These are the kings of the land whom the Israelites had defeated and whose territory they took over east of the Jordan, from the Arnon Gorge to Mount Hermon, including all the eastern side of the Arabah - Josh 12:1 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Chapter 12 is a list. It is a careful, official record of the kings Israel defeated and the land they took — first the territory east of the Jordan, then, in the verses to come, the long roll of kings west of it. At first glance a chapter of names and boundaries can feel like the least inspiring page in the Bible. But pause and ask why the writer bothered to record it at all.

This is a memorial. It is Israel's way of saying: look what God has done. Every king named here once stood as an obstacle, a threat, a reason to be afraid. Now each one is written down as defeated. The list is not boasting in Israel's strength; it is a testimony to God's faithfulness, victory by victory.

There is wisdom in keeping such records. We forget so quickly. The fear that gripped us last year, the mountain we were sure we could not climb, the prayer we were certain would go unanswered — how easily we lose track of the God who carried us through. Scripture repeatedly urges God's people to remember, to write it down, to tell the next generation (Ps 78:4). Keeping a record of God's faithfulness is one of the simplest ways to strengthen our faith for the battles still ahead.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- What victories has God given you that you have half-forgotten?
- Would it help to keep a written record of God's faithfulness in your life?
- How does remembering the past strengthen you for what lies ahead?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, I forget so easily all that You have done. Help me to remember Your faithfulness and to tell of Your goodness to those who come after me. Amen.
